skill.name: gregstyle-hyperframes
skill.description: Use when creating Greg-style HyperFrames videos in 9:16 or 16:9: researched, visual-first explainers with sourced public images, extremely sparse copy, center-weighted poster compositions, GSAP motion, visual QA, and rendered MP4 output.
whenToUse: Creating or recreating a short Greg-style HyperFrames visual video from a topic, reference screenshots, or local design references
Making a researched, public-asset-based 9:16 or 16:9 explainer about real people, products, companies, or places
Iterating a HyperFrames composition toward center-weighted poster layouts with large imagery and sparse copy
Validating and rendering a local HyperFrames project into a polished MP4 with a per-scene contact sheet

keyConcepts.explanation: A 12-18 second, 30fps social video at 1080x1920 (default) or 1920x1080, with off-white paper texture, subtle radial light, dot grain, heavy-bordered cards, geometric blocks, dashed connector diagrams, and a fixed palette (ink #16241f, paper #eee9df, mint #66b79a, coral #c84a35, gold #e2b54c).

Every frame should read like an editorial poster at thumbnail size. Keep the focal composition in the central 70% of the canvas, let the visual object (portrait, logo, product image, diagram) dominate over copy, preserve generous negative space, and never let edge elements carry the main idea.

When the video depends on real people, products, companies, places, or current facts, research reliable sources (official pages, Wikimedia, reputable publications), download usable images into assets/<topic>/, use local paths in the composition, and report source URLs in the final response.

Most 15-second videos use four scenes: a poster opener (thesis plus central motif), a hero comparison (two large image-led cards), a pattern map (one centered 3-4 node diagram), and a closing thesis with up to three watch items. One idea per scene, target 12 visible words or fewer per scene with a hard maximum of 20.

The active index.html defines one root composition with data-composition-id="main", data-start="0", data-fps="30", and data-width/data-height matching the aspect ratio; GSAP motion registers on window.__timelines["main"].

After building, run npm run check, render with npm run render, extract representative frames with ffmpeg, and build a contact sheet with one settled frame per scene chosen from actual scene timings. Patch and rerender if any scene is blank, off-center, too wordy, visually timid, clipped, or unclear.

apiReference.signature: Preserve current index.html before replacing it
apiReference.purpose: Before editing, inspect the workspace and copy the current active composition into variants/ so the prior version can be recovered; reuse the project's existing patterns, duration, dimensions, naming, and render scripts.
Use a single main composition root with fixed dimensions and 30fps timing; 1080x1920 for 9:16 (default) or 1920x1080 for 16:9.

Register GSAP motion on the main HyperFrames timeline: reveal kicker/headline from a slight vertical offset, bring cards in with scale/y/small rotation using back.out, draw lines with scaleX from 0, add one slow living pulse, and fade each scene out in the final 0.2s.
apiReference.example:
window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};
window.__timelines["main"] = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });

apiReference.purpose: Run HyperFrames lint, validation, and inspection checks before rendering; fix structural and layout issues, treating contrast warnings as judgment calls for stylized editorial pieces unless readability is clearly poor.
Render the validated HyperFrames composition to MP4, then copy the latest render to a descriptive top-level filename.
Extract representative frames after rendering and assemble a per-scene contact sheet so layout, centering, copy density, and blank scenes can be inspected.

gotchas: Preserve the current active index.html in variants/ before replacing it.
Use local images under assets/<topic>/ in the composition; avoid remote image URLs.

Keep all primary content center-weighted inside the safe area (roughly 110-130px from left/right, 120-140px from top, 120px from bottom); reject layouts with large dead zones, tiny cards, long subheads, or text spread across the whole canvas.
Scale visual assets assertively: paired 16:9 cards should usually occupy about 60-75% of canvas width and 50-65% of its height.

Keep copy minimal: headlines 2-6 words, kickers 3-6 words, cards limited to a name plus one proof point, diagram nodes 1-3 words per line, takeaway chips 1-2 words; target 12 visible words per scene, hard maximum 20.
Prefer one idea per scene; do not shrink text to fit a second idea, and use scale, color blocks, borders, and whitespace for contrast instead of extra paragraphs.
Add position: absolute to every map or card element that uses left, right, top, or bottom.
Avoid duplicate image source/start/duration warnings by copying reused images to alternate local filenames when needed.
Choose contact-sheet timestamps from actual scene timings rather than generic frame numbers.
Patch and rerender if any extracted preview frame is blank, off-center, clipped, too wordy, visually timid, or unclear.
